picks.title: Opinion: If the AI bubble bursts, it could create a serious problem for health care
picks.take: A health AI company's market value and the medical value of its technology are two different things, which is news only to anyone who has never read a prospectus. Clinicians may soon learn which workflows were load-bearing and which were venture-funded.

picks.title: Epic Systems defends competitive practices, promises to let AI access its records
picks.take: Epic defended its competitive practices at a conference, then promised AI access to its records. Medicine's data gatekeeper is now enthusiastic about openness, as soon as the term is defined internally.

picks.title: The emerging winners and losers in the AI scribe market
picks.take: The AI scribe market is sorting into winners and losers, which is progress for a field where documentation burden was supposed to be solved three funding rounds ago. Clinicians await the part where the notes get shorter.

picks.title: What to know about the new AI roadmap from CMS, and news from HLTH
picks.take: CMS has released an AI roadmap, giving the industry a rare chance to check whether the destination includes anything resembling reimbursement logic. Physicians will be pleased to learn the map exists. The terrain remains prior authorization.

picks.title: AI chatbots and youth suicide risk: current evidence, critical gaps, and a clinical research agenda
picks.take: A review of AI chatbots and youth suicide risk finds critical evidence gaps and proposes a clinical research agenda. The products shipped first, and the research agenda arrives to examine them, as is tradition.

picks.title: Verifiable summarization of electronic health records using large language models to support chart review
picks.take: Researchers are working on summaries of electronic health records that can be verified against the chart. This is a refreshing standard for a technology whose usual pitch is that you should simply trust the confident paragraph.

picks.title: Bias and equity in large language model-based applications for health care: a scoping review
picks.take: A scoping review of bias and equity in LLM-based health applications arrives just as deployment is accelerating. Equity assessment remains the seatbelt installed after the car has been sold, test-driven, and recommended to your cardiologist.

picks.title: AI and affordability steal the show: 6 takeaways from HLTH
picks.take: HLTH takeaways: AI and affordability stole the show. Two topics are bound to share a stage at a conference where the first is usually priced, and the second is mostly discussed.

picks.title: Benchmarking and developing large language models using one million clinical trials
picks.take: A benchmark built from one million clinical trials tests whether language models can handle the trial literature. Medicine has finally produced a data set large enough that nobody, including the investigators' mothers, has read all of it.

picks.title: Generative AI mental health chatbots: a scoping review of intervention design and user experience
picks.take: A scoping review of generative AI mental health chatbots examines intervention design and user experience. Access to care is scarce, so we have built a patient, tireless, unlicensed listener, and now we are, appropriately, reading the manual.
